extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research-integrity professionals, science journalists, and interested members of the public
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and documenting instances of alleged or confirmed scientific misconduct, retractions, and institutional/ORI findings; highlighting what went wrong in research practice and publication. Focus is on describing behaviors that constitute misconduct and the consequences (retractions, investigations, resignations, corrections, replications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data manipulation / changed data
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances in which a researcher 'changed data so that it would show a desired effect.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an explicit example of wrongdoing — altering primary data to produce preferred results is a core form of scientific misconduct. The page cites the 85-page report detailing such instances as evidence for ORI findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation of results / shading of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'disturbing pattern of misrepresentation of results and shading of truth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrays selective or misleading presentation of findings (omitting inconvenient facts, framing results to exaggerate effects) as a serious breach of scientific standards. Anti-patterns include wording or presentation that gives a false impression of the strength, scope, or provenance of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reckless disregard for basic scientific standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The report characterizes behavior as a 'reckless disregard for basic scientific standards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad standard encompassing failure to follow accepted research methods, record-keeping, oversight, ethical practices, or quality controls. Use as a catch-all for patterns of behavior that systematically violate norms (e.g., poor documentation, lack of verification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to internal concerns / rebuffing lab questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The researcher 'more than once rebuffed or downplayed questions and concerns from people in his laboratory about how a result was obtained.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how senior researchers handle internal critiques and whistleblowing: ignoring, dismissing, or intimidating lab members is an indicator of problematic research culture and possible misconduct. Positive practice: investigate and transparently address concerns raised by colleagues or trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of publication record / disclosure of retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting that Hauser 'hadn’t even bothered to note in his list of publications that one of his papers had been retracted.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should keep accurate, up-to-date publication lists that disclose retractions, corrections, or expressions of concern. Omitting such notices is an ethical lapse and undermines transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional and ORI determinations of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings that the researcher was 'found guilty of misconduct by the Office of Research Integrity (ORI)' and that Harvard sent a report to the ORI documenting issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes formal investigations and determinations by institutions and oversight bodies as key standards for judging research integrity. Such reports provide baseline evidence for misconduct claims and list specific substantiated behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of misconduct across funded grants
rubrics_metrics.description: The report covered 'misconduct in four different NIH grants.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether problematic practices affect multiple projects or funding sources; broad scope increases severity and has implications for grant oversight, corrective actions, and reporting to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication / reproducibility as corrective test
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage noting that a replication published in Science 'shows that results published in the journal in 2007 ... have held up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful independent replication is treated as evidence that some published findings are robust despite surrounding misconduct allegations; replication is a key standard for validating results when questions arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal handling of retractions and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention that a journal's 'retraction ... was, by the editors’ own admission, handled badly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates journals on timeliness, transparency, and adequacy of handling retractions, corrections, and editorial communications. Poor editorial handling exacerbates harm from problematic research and undermines trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author acknowledgement / acceptance of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A retraction notice included 'MH accepts responsibility for the error.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether authors acknowledge errors or accept responsibility is an indicator of ethical conduct post-discovery. Transparent admission and corrective steps (corrections, retractions, notifications) are expected practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public communication and transparency about investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Freedom of Information Act request to obtain the Harvard report and public reporting (Boston Globe, Retraction Watch) on investigative findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access to investigative reports, timely press coverage, and sharing of findings improve accountability. Lack of transparency (withholding reports or details) is an anti-pattern that impedes community assessment.
